info.title: KNOWALL — Module 1 API
info.description: Single-society demo backend. Module 2 Notice V1 adds official notices for a verified Society Admin and currently eligible residents. Eligible residents can also create society discussions, threaded comments, and suggestions through society.notices.read. No separate discussion or suggestion permission is registered. Suggestion status stays SUBMITTED; committee decisions, reporting, and moderation are not implemented. Eligible residents can read a safe governance history of published notices, discussions, and suggestions from the existing audit log. All state-changing /api operations require an X-CSRF-Token from GET /api/auth/csrf. The session cookie is HttpOnly and stored by the browser. Use GET /api/auth/csrf before login and again after login (login rotates the CSRF token). Swagger UI cannot set browser authentication cookies manually: execute login in the same Swagger origin, then try protected endpoints. Demo console email links are development-only. Phase 6 adds draft/submission and invitation APIs. Pending applications DO NOT confer resident rights. Phase 7 adds private document upload and on-demand OCR; Phase 8 adds human administrator approvals, correction/rejection workflows, memberships and audit history. Enhancement: optional personal details, sponsored-family relationship, household family tree and administrator-confirmed current occupancy. No voting system is added. Family administrator review enhancement: explicit, live sponsor_context and advisory OCR-to-sponsor name comparison. No automatic family relationship validation or eligibility based on occupancy.

get.description: Returns current user roles, verified active memberships and effective permission codes. Permissions are display hints to the frontend, never authority for a Flask endpoint. Owner/tenant/family is a membership category rather than a permission role. Access can change immediately after suspension, expiry, sponsor ineligibility or revocation. Future-module permission names indicate shared capability contracts only; each module must also enforce resource-specific eligibility.
